title: What is the EU AI Act?
description: Introduction to the world's first comprehensive AI regulation.
snippet: By the end of this chapter, you will be able to: - Explain the purpose and legal basis of the EU AI Act - Describe the six key policy objectives driving this regulation - Understand the risk-based regulatory philosophy - Identify where the AI Act sits in the broader EU regulatory landscape - Recognize the global significance of this first-of-its-kind regulation --- The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) represents a watershed moment in technology regulation. Adopted on 13 June 2024 and entering into force on 1 August 2024, it is the world's first comprehensive legal framework specifically designed to govern artificial intelligence throughout its lifecycle. The AI Act was proposed by the European Commission on 21 April 2021 as part of its broader digital strategy. snippet: By the end of this chapter, you will be able to: - Precisely define what constitutes an "AI system" under the regulation - Distinguish between the six categories of actors in the AI value chain - Understand critical lifecycle concepts (placing on market, putting into service) - Identify when substantial modifications trigger new compliance obligations - Apply definitions accurately in compliance assessments --- Article 3 of the AI Act contains 68 legal definitions that form the interpretive foundation of the entire regulation. title: Record-Keeping and Logging
description: Article 12 automatic logging capabilities.
snippet: By the end of this chapter, you will be able to: - Design AI logging systems that meet Article 12 requirements - Determine appropriate log retention periods for different contexts - Implement technical controls for log integrity and accessibility - Establish logging procedures for different actor types - Integrate logging with incident investigation and post-market monitoring --- Article 12 mandates automatic logging capabilities for high-risk AI systems. Logs serve as the "flight recorder" for AI—enabling traceability, accountability, incident investigation, and regulatory oversight throughout the system's operational life. Logs provide an audit trail of AI system operations, enabling reconstruction of what happened, when, and why. When issues arise, logs identify who was involved and what decisions were made. Authorities use logs to investigate incidents and verify ongoing compliance. Post-market monitoring relies on log data to identify performance issues. --- High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system. Key elements: - Automatic: Logging must be built into the system, not manual - Events: System activities and decisions must be captured - Lifetime: From deployment through decommissioning Logging capabilities must ensure traceability appropriate to the intended purpose: Intended Purpose Traceability Level Example Logs

title: Accuracy, Robustness, and Cybersecurity
description: Article 15 technical performance requirements.
snippet: By the end of this chapter, you will be able to: - Define accuracy metrics appropriate for different AI system types - Design robustness strategies including redundancy and fail-safe mechanisms - Identify and mitigate AI-specific cybersecurity threats - Implement testing frameworks for ongoing performance validation - Document accuracy levels in compliance with disclosure requirements --- Article 15 establishes the technical performance requirements that ensure high-risk AI systems operate reliably, safely, and securely throughout their lifecycle. title: Chapter III - High-Risk AI Systems
description: EU AI Act: Chapter III - High-Risk AI Systems
snippet: Training Note: This is the most extensive chapter, covering the requirements for high-risk AI systems. It details classification criteria, obligations for providers and deployers, conformity assessment procedures, and technical documentation requirements. title: AI System
description: A machine-based system designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy, that may exhibit adaptiveness after deployment and that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments.

snippet: A natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body using an AI system under its authority except where the AI system is used in the course of a personal non-professional activity.

title: Authorised Representative
description: A natural or legal person located or established in the Union who has received and accepted a written mandate from a provider of an AI system or a general-purpose AI model to, respectively, perform and carry out on its behalf the obligations and procedures established by this Regulation.
snippet: A natural or legal person located or established in the Union who has received and accepted a written mandate from a provider of an AI system or a general-purpose AI model to, respectively, perform and carry out on its behalf the obligations and procedures established by this Regulation.

title: Importer
description: A natural or legal person located or established in the Union that places on the market an AI system that bears the name or trademark of a natural or legal person established in a third country.
snippet: A natural or legal person located or established in the Union that places on the market an AI system that bears the name or trademark of a natural or legal person established in a third country.

title: Distributor
description: A natural or legal person in the supply chain, other than the provider or the importer, that makes an AI system available on the Union market.
snippet: A natural or legal person in the supply chain, other than the provider or the importer, that makes an AI system available on the Union market.

title: Operator
description: A provider, product manufacturer, deployer, authorised representative, importer or distributor.
snippet: A provider, product manufacturer, deployer, authorised representative, importer or distributor.

title: Affected Person
description: A natural person who is subject to or otherwise affected by an AI system.
snippet: A natural person who is subject to or otherwise affected by an AI system.

title: Notified Body
description: A conformity assessment body notified in accordance with this Regulation and other relevant Union harmonisation legislation.
snippet: A conformity assessment body notified in accordance with this Regulation and other relevant Union harmonisation legislation.

title: Prohibited AI Practices
description: AI systems and practices that are prohibited under Article 5 due to their unacceptable risk to fundamental rights, including subliminal manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring by public authorities, and certain uses of real-time remote biometric identification.
snippet: AI systems and practices that are prohibited under Article 5 due to their unacceptable risk to fundamental rights, including subliminal manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring by public authorities, and certain uses of real-time remote biometric identification.

title: High-Risk AI System
description: An AI system that falls within one of the areas listed in Annex III (such as biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration, justice) or is a safety component of a product covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I.
snippet: An AI system that falls within one of the areas listed in Annex III (such as biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration, justice) or is a safety component of a product covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I.

title: Limited Risk AI
description: AI systems subject primarily to transparency obligations under Article 50, where users must be informed they are interacting with AI or that content was AI-generated.
snippet: AI systems subject primarily to transparency obligations under Article 50, where users must be informed they are interacting with AI or that content was AI-generated.

title: Minimal Risk AI
description: AI systems not falling under prohibited, high-risk, or limited risk categories. No mandatory requirements apply, though voluntary codes of conduct are encouraged.
snippet: AI systems not falling under prohibited, high-risk, or limited risk categories. No mandatory requirements apply, though voluntary codes of conduct are encouraged.

title: Social Scoring
description: AI systems that evaluate or classify natural persons or groups based on their social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal characteristics, leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment in unrelated social contexts or disproportionate to their social behaviour.
snippet: AI systems that evaluate or classify natural persons or groups based on their social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal characteristics, leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment in unrelated social contexts or disproportionate to their social behaviour.

title: Subliminal Techniques
description: AI systems deploying techniques beyond a person's consciousness to materially distort their behaviour in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause significant harm.
snippet: AI systems deploying techniques beyond a person's consciousness to materially distort their behaviour in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause significant harm.

title: Biometric Identification
description: The automated recognition of physical, physiological, behavioural, or psychological human features for the purpose of establishing the identity of a natural person by comparing biometric data of that person to biometric data stored in a database.
snippet: The automated recognition of physical, physiological, behavioural, or psychological human features for the purpose of establishing the identity of a natural person by comparing biometric data of that person to biometric data stored in a database.

title: Remote Biometric Identification
description: An AI system for the purpose of identifying natural persons, without their active involvement, typically at a distance through comparison of a person's biometric data with the biometric data contained in a reference database.
snippet: An AI system for the purpose of identifying natural persons, without their active involvement, typically at a distance through comparison of a person's biometric data with the biometric data contained in a reference database.

title: Real-Time Remote Biometric Identification
description: A remote biometric identification system whereby the capturing of biometric data, the comparison and the identification all occur without a significant delay, comprising instantaneous identification as well as limited short delays to avoid circumvention.
snippet: A remote biometric identification system whereby the capturing of biometric data, the comparison and the identification all occur without a significant delay, comprising instantaneous identification as well as limited short delays to avoid circumvention.

title: Post Remote Biometric Identification
description: A remote biometric identification system other than a real-time remote biometric identification system.
snippet: A remote biometric identification system other than a real-time remote biometric identification system.

title: Emotion Recognition System
description: An AI system for the purpose of identifying or inferring emotions or intentions of natural persons on the basis of their biometric data.
snippet: An AI system for the purpose of identifying or inferring emotions or intentions of natural persons on the basis of their biometric data.

title: Biometric Categorisation System
description: An AI system for the purpose of assigning natural persons to specific categories on the basis of their biometric data, unless ancillary to another commercial service and strictly necessary for objective technical reasons.
snippet: An AI system for the purpose of assigning natural persons to specific categories on the basis of their biometric data, unless ancillary to another commercial service and strictly necessary for objective technical reasons.

title: Conformity Assessment
description: The process demonstrating whether the requirements of this Regulation relating to a high-risk AI system have been fulfilled. Conformity assessment may be based on internal control or involve a third-party assessment by a notified body.
snippet: The process demonstrating whether the requirements of this Regulation relating to a high-risk AI system have been fulfilled. Conformity assessment may be based on internal control or involve a third-party assessment by a notified body.

title: CE Marking
description: A marking by which a provider indicates that an AI system is in conformity with the requirements of this Regulation and other applicable Union harmonisation legislation providing for its affixing.
snippet: A marking by which a provider indicates that an AI system is in conformity with the requirements of this Regulation and other applicable Union harmonisation legislation providing for its affixing.

title: EU Declaration of Conformity
description: A document drawn up by the provider stating that the high-risk AI system complies with the requirements of this Regulation. The declaration must be kept for 10 years after the AI system has been placed on the market.
snippet: A document drawn up by the provider stating that the high-risk AI system complies with the requirements of this Regulation. The declaration must be kept for 10 years after the AI system has been placed on the market.

title: Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (FRIA)
description: An assessment carried out by deployers of high-risk AI systems that are bodies governed by public law, or private entities providing public services, and deployers using AI for credit scoring or risk assessment in life/health insurance.
snippet: An assessment carried out by deployers of high-risk AI systems that are bodies governed by public law, or private entities providing public services, and deployers using AI for credit scoring or risk assessment in life/health insurance.

title: Quality Management System
description: A system implemented by providers of high-risk AI systems to ensure compliance with this Regulation, documented in a systematic and orderly manner in the form of written policies, procedures and instructions.
snippet: A system implemented by providers of high-risk AI systems to ensure compliance with this Regulation, documented in a systematic and orderly manner in the form of written policies, procedures and instructions.

title: Post-Market Monitoring
description: All activities carried out by providers of AI systems to collect and review experience gained from the use of AI systems they place on the market or put into service for the purpose of identifying any need to immediately apply corrective or preventive actions.
snippet: All activities carried out by providers of AI systems to collect and review experience gained from the use of AI systems they place on the market or put into service for the purpose of identifying any need to immediately apply corrective or preventive actions.

title: AI Regulatory Sandbox
description: A controlled framework set up by a competent authority which offers providers or prospective providers of AI systems the possibility to develop, train, validate and test an innovative AI system under regulatory supervision for a limited time.
snippet: A controlled framework set up by a competent authority which offers providers or prospective providers of AI systems the possibility to develop, train, validate and test an innovative AI system under regulatory supervision for a limited time.

title: Harmonised Standard
description: A European standard adopted on the basis of a request made by the Commission for the application of Union harmonisation legislation.
snippet: A European standard adopted on the basis of a request made by the Commission for the application of Union harmonisation legislation.

title: Common Specification
description: A set of technical specifications providing means to comply with certain requirements established under this Regulation, adopted by the Commission where harmonised standards do not exist or are insufficient.
snippet: A set of technical specifications providing means to comply with certain requirements established under this Regulation, adopted by the Commission where harmonised standards do not exist or are insufficient.

title: Technical Documentation
description: Documentation required under Article 11 that enables national competent authorities and notified bodies to assess the compliance of the high-risk AI system with the requirements set out in this Regulation.
snippet: Documentation required under Article 11 that enables national competent authorities and notified bodies to assess the compliance of the high-risk AI system with the requirements set out in this Regulation.

title: Instructions for Use
description: Information provided by the provider to inform the deployer of an AI system's intended purpose and proper use, including the specific geographical, behavioural or functional settings within which the high-risk AI system is intended to be used.
snippet: Information provided by the provider to inform the deployer of an AI system's intended purpose and proper use, including the specific geographical, behavioural or functional settings within which the high-risk AI system is intended to be used.

title: Logging Capabilities
description: Automatic recording of events (logs) while high-risk AI systems are operating, enabling traceability of the AI system's functioning throughout its lifecycle.
snippet: Automatic recording of events (logs) while high-risk AI systems are operating, enabling traceability of the AI system's functioning throughout its lifecycle.

title: EU Database for High-Risk AI Systems
description: A database established and maintained by the Commission containing information about high-risk AI systems registered by providers before placing them on the market or putting them into service.
snippet: A database established and maintained by the Commission containing information about high-risk AI systems registered by providers before placing them on the market or putting them into service.

title: Risk Management System
description: A continuous iterative process planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle of a high-risk AI system, requiring regular systematic updating. It shall identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks, estimate and evaluate risks, and adopt risk management measures.
snippet: A continuous iterative process planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle of a high-risk AI system, requiring regular systematic updating. It shall identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks, estimate and evaluate risks, and adopt risk management measures.

title: Data Governance
description: Requirements for training, validation and testing data sets used for high-risk AI systems, including requirements for relevance, representativeness, accuracy, completeness, and appropriateness for the intended purpose.
snippet: Requirements for training, validation and testing data sets used for high-risk AI systems, including requirements for relevance, representativeness, accuracy, completeness, and appropriateness for the intended purpose.

title: Human Oversight
description: Measures designed to be implemented by the deployer, or identified by the provider, to enable natural persons to oversee the functioning of a high-risk AI system, understand its capabilities and limitations, monitor operation, and intervene or interrupt when necessary.
snippet: Measures designed to be implemented by the deployer, or identified by the provider, to enable natural persons to oversee the functioning of a high-risk AI system, understand its capabilities and limitations, monitor operation, and intervene or interrupt when necessary.

title: Accuracy
description: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, as declared by the provider.
snippet: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, as declared by the provider.

title: Robustness
description: The ability of a high-risk AI system to maintain its level of performance when facing conditions not anticipated during development, including errors, faults, inconsistencies, or adversarial attacks.
snippet: The ability of a high-risk AI system to maintain its level of performance when facing conditions not anticipated during development, including errors, faults, inconsistencies, or adversarial attacks.

title: Cybersecurity
description: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed so that they achieve an appropriate level of cybersecurity and are resilient against attempts to alter their use, outputs or performance.
snippet: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed so that they achieve an appropriate level of cybersecurity and are resilient against attempts to alter their use, outputs or performance.

title: Transparency Requirements
description: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way as to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system's output and use it appropriately.
snippet: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way as to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system's output and use it appropriately.

title: AI Office
description: The Commission body established to support the implementation and enforcement of the AI Act, particularly regarding general-purpose AI models, and to coordinate AI governance across the EU.
snippet: The Commission body established to support the implementation and enforcement of the AI Act, particularly regarding general-purpose AI models, and to coordinate AI governance across the EU.

title: European Artificial Intelligence Board
description: An advisory body composed of representatives from Member States established to assist the Commission and Member States in ensuring consistent application of the AI Act across the Union.
snippet: An advisory body composed of representatives from Member States established to assist the Commission and Member States in ensuring consistent application of the AI Act across the Union.

title: National Competent Authority
description: The notifying authority and the market surveillance authority designated by each Member State for the purpose of the AI Act. Member States may designate more than one competent authority.
snippet: The notifying authority and the market surveillance authority designated by each Member State for the purpose of the AI Act. Member States may designate more than one competent authority.

title: Market Surveillance Authority
description: The national authority carrying out market surveillance activities and enforcement of the AI Act, with powers to investigate, request information, and take corrective measures.
snippet: The national authority carrying out market surveillance activities and enforcement of the AI Act, with powers to investigate, request information, and take corrective measures.

title: Scientific Panel of Independent Experts
description: A panel of independent experts established to support the enforcement of the AI Act, particularly in relation to general-purpose AI models, providing technical expertise and assessments.
snippet: A panel of independent experts established to support the enforcement of the AI Act, particularly in relation to general-purpose AI models, providing technical expertise and assessments.

title: Training Data
description: Data used for training an AI system through fitting its learnable parameters. Training data must meet quality requirements for high-risk AI systems.
snippet: Data used for training an AI system through fitting its learnable parameters. Training data must meet quality requirements for high-risk AI systems.

title: Validation Data
description: Data used for providing an evaluation of the trained AI system and for tuning its non-learnable parameters and its learning process to prevent underfitting or overfitting.
snippet: Data used for providing an evaluation of the trained AI system and for tuning its non-learnable parameters and its learning process to prevent underfitting or overfitting.

title: Testing Data
description: Data used for providing an independent evaluation of the AI system to confirm expected performance before placing on the market or putting into service.
snippet: Data used for providing an independent evaluation of the AI system to confirm expected performance before placing on the market or putting into service.

title: Input Data
description: Data provided to or directly acquired by an AI system on the basis of which the system produces an output.
snippet: Data provided to or directly acquired by an AI system on the basis of which the system produces an output.

title: Biometric Data
description: Personal data resulting from specific technical processing relating to the physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics of a natural person, such as facial images or dactyloscopic data.
snippet: Personal data resulting from specific technical processing relating to the physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics of a natural person, such as facial images or dactyloscopic data.

title: Deep Fake
description: AI-generated or manipulated image, audio or video content that resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear to a person to be authentic or truthful.
snippet: AI-generated or manipulated image, audio or video content that resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear to a person to be authentic or truthful.

title: Serious Incident
description: An incident or malfunctioning of an AI system that directly or indirectly leads to death or serious damage to health, property, or the environment, or serious and irreversible disruption of critical infrastructure.
snippet: An incident or malfunctioning of an AI system that directly or indirectly leads to death or serious damage to health, property, or the environment, or serious and irreversible disruption of critical infrastructure.

title: Penalties and Fines
description: Administrative fines for non-compliance with the AI Act, with maximum amounts up to 35 million EUR or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for prohibited AI practices, 15 million EUR or 3% for other violations.
snippet: Administrative fines for non-compliance with the AI Act, with maximum amounts up to 35 million EUR or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for prohibited AI practices, 15 million EUR or 3% for other violations.

title: Right to Explanation
description: The right of affected persons to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations about the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken.
snippet: The right of affected persons to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations about the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken.

title: Right to Lodge a Complaint
description: The right of any natural or legal person to lodge a complaint with the relevant market surveillance authority if they consider that there has been an infringement of the AI Act.
snippet: The right of any natural or legal person to lodge a complaint with the relevant market surveillance authority if they consider that there has been an infringement of the AI Act.

title: General-Purpose AI Model
description: An AI model, including where such an AI model is trained with a large amount of data using self-supervision at scale, that displays significant generality and is capable of competently performing a wide range of distinct tasks.
snippet: An AI model, including where such an AI model is trained with a large amount of data using self-supervision at scale, that displays significant generality and is capable of competently performing a wide range of distinct tasks.

title: General-Purpose AI Model with Systemic Risk
description: A general-purpose AI model that has high impact capabilities evaluated on the basis of appropriate technical tools and methodologies, including indicators such as computational power used for training (threshold: 10^25 FLOP).
snippet: A general-purpose AI model that has high impact capabilities evaluated on the basis of appropriate technical tools and methodologies, including indicators such as computational power used for training (threshold: 10^25 FLOP).

title: Systemic Risk
description: A risk that is specific to the high-impact capabilities of general-purpose AI models, having a significant impact on the Union market due to their reach, or due to actual or reasonably foreseeable negative effects on public health, safety, public security, fundamental rights, or society.
snippet: A risk that is specific to the high-impact capabilities of general-purpose AI models, having a significant impact on the Union market due to their reach, or due to actual or reasonably foreseeable negative effects on public health, safety, public security, fundamental rights, or society.

title: Downstream Provider
description: A provider of an AI system, including a general-purpose AI system, which integrates an AI model, regardless of whether the AI model is provided by themselves and vertically integrated or provided by another entity based on contractual relations.
snippet: A provider of an AI system, including a general-purpose AI system, which integrates an AI model, regardless of whether the AI model is provided by themselves and vertically integrated or provided by another entity based on contractual relations.

title: GPAI Transparency Obligations
description: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models to draw up and keep up-to-date technical documentation, make available information to downstream providers, put in place a policy to respect EU copyright law, and publish a summary of training data.
snippet: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models to draw up and keep up-to-date technical documentation, make available information to downstream providers, put in place a policy to respect EU copyright law, and publish a summary of training data.

title: Model Evaluation
description: Evaluations of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to identify and mitigate systemic risks, including adversarial testing and red-teaming procedures.
snippet: Evaluations of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to identify and mitigate systemic risks, including adversarial testing and red-teaming procedures.

title: Codes of Practice
description: Voluntary codes developed with the involvement of providers of general-purpose AI models to demonstrate compliance with GPAI obligations, providing detailed technical and operational guidance.
snippet: Voluntary codes developed with the involvement of providers of general-purpose AI models to demonstrate compliance with GPAI obligations, providing detailed technical and operational guidance.

title: What is the EU AI Act?
description: The EU AI Act is the world's first comprehensive legal framework for artificial intelligence. It establishes a risk-based approach to regulating AI systems, categorizing them into four risk levels: prohibited, high-risk, limited risk, and minimal risk. The regulation aims to ensure AI systems in the EU are safe, transparent, traceable, non-discriminatory, and environmentally friendly.

• August 2, 2025: Requirements for general-purpose AI models
• August 2, 2026: Full application of high-risk AI system requirements
• August 2, 2027: Requirements for certain high-risk AI systems in Annex I

title: Does the EU AI Act apply to my organization?
description:
The EU AI Act applies to:

• Providers (developers) of AI systems placed on the EU market
• Deployers (users) of AI systems within the EU
• Providers and deployers outside the EU whose AI systems are used in the EU
• Importers and distributors of AI systems

The Act applies regardless of whether the organization is based in the EU, as long as the AI system affects people in the EU.

title: What are the penalties for non-compliance?
description:
The EU AI Act establishes significant penalties for non-compliance:

• Up to €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover for prohibited AI practices
• Up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover for other violations
• Up to €7.5 million or 1.5% of global annual turnover for providing incorrect information

For SMEs and startups, the lower of the two amounts applies. Member States may also impose additional penalties.

• Biometric categorization based on sensitive attributes
• Predictive policing based solely on profiling

title: How do I determine the risk classification of my AI system?
description:
To determine risk classification:

1. First check if your AI system falls under prohibited practices (Article 5)
2. Check if it's a safety component of products in Annex I
3. Check if it falls into high-risk categories in Annex III
4. If not high-risk, check if it has transparency obligations (chatbots, deepfakes, emotion recognition)
5. If none of the above, it's likely minimal risk

We recommend using our Risk Classification Assessment tool for a guided evaluation.
